messages:
maria: hey @support, after upgrading the python SDK to 0.4.1 my app crashes at import time: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'
sam: can you paste the pip/poetry commands you used to install? also which python (pyenv/venv) are you on?
maria: using poetry, python 3.11 (pyenv). I ran:
```
poetry add redwood-sdk@0.4.1
poetry install
```
then `poetry run python -c 'import redwood'` -> ModuleNotFoundError
tony: did you add it as a dev dependency by accident? `poetry add --dev` would skip it in non-dev installs
maria: i checked pyproject.toml, it's under [tool.poetry.dependencies] correctly. not dev.
support-bot: quick checks: run `poetry run python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable, sys.path)"` and `poetry run python -m pip show redwood-sdk` to confirm installed package path
maria: output: ```/Users/maria/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/myproj-py3.11/bin/python ['...', '/Users/maria/myproj']```
`pip show redwood-sdk` => WARNING: Package(s) not found: redwood-sdk
sam: odd. run `poetry run pip list | grep redwood` and `poetry lock && poetry install --no-root` to ensure lock matches
maria: `poetry run pip list` shows redwood==0.4.1 but package name is `redwood` not `redwood-sdk`? my import is `import redwood` in code. error still ModuleNotFoundError though
tony: maybe package was installed but under different egg name, or package has different top-level module. try `poetry run python -c "import importlib; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood'))"`
maria: returns None
devex: do you have any editable installs or local path overrides in pyproject? editable mode (poetry install --editable) doesn't always expose extras. also check `poetry export -f requirements.txt --dev --without-hashes` and inspect
maria: i have a local editable during development: `[tool.poetry.dependencies]
redwood = {path = "../redwood", develop = true}`
maybe that's the culprit
sam: when using path dependency in develop mode, poetry doesn't necessarily build/install the package unless you run `poetry install --no-root` or `pip install -e ../redwood[async]` to include extras. if the package metadata doesn't expose the top-level module (bad setup.cfg/pyproject) import can fail
maria: the local package does have a pyproject, but i forgot to include `packages = find:` in setup.cfg when testing with editable. the wheel build adds the package but editable didn't. argh
tony: easy repro steps others can try: 1) clone repo, 2) set pyenv 3.11, 3) poetry install, 4) poetry run python -c "import redwood" -> fail. if that's reproducible, try `poetry run pip install -e ../redwood` and see if import works
maria: i did `poetry run pip install -e ../redwood[async]` and now `import redwood` works. also discovered during run that httpx import failed earlier because httpx pinned at 0.18 from another dep; adding the extras pulled httpx>=0.23 which resolved `cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'httpx'`
support-bot: resolution checklist: 1) avoid relying on develop path dependency for CI/SMOKE; 2) if using path/develop, ensure packaging metadata includes packages/find; 3) install extras explicitly for editable installs `pip install -e .[async]`; 4) pin/conflict-check transitive deps `poetry show --tree httpx`
maria: thanks all. i'll update the pyproject in the local package and add a note in CONTRIBUTING about installing extras in dev mode. saved my morning :coffee:
sam: sweet, if you can paste a minimal repro (repo link + exact commands) we'll add a short note to support KB
maria: will do in a bit, linking here when ready
